newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares edge up 0.31 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares edge up 0.31 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended slightly firmer on Friday amid selective and narrow trade, despite earlier profit-taking, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at this week's fourth all-time high of 1,918, up six points, or 0.31 percent from Thursday's previous record of 1,912.
Today's was the sixth record since late June when hopes of a secularist coalition boosted the market.
The index also brushed a trading record of 1,936 in the morning.
Over the week, it gained 5.67 percent on top of last week's 10.5 percent surge prompted by political optimism.
A right-left coalition headed by conservative Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz was formed on Monday, to replace the former Islamist-led coalition.
Expectations that the new government will win a confidence vote in parliament on July 12 are widespread.
Trade volume firmed to 29.69 trillion lira from Thursday's 27.48 trillion.

"Selective activity was dominant today with shares having less premiums coming in focus. But in general, the market drifted sideways in weak volume. I expect trade to be better next week," said Mesut Ozdinc from Oyak securities.

"The market will be positively affected if any more deputy defections from the Islamist-conservative opposition occur. The index may test 2,000 levels unless negative political news come up," he added.

Yilmaz has predicted that his government will win the confidence vote with a bigger-than-expected majority with the help of the latest series of MP defections from former Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare party and its conservative ally Tansu Ciller's True Path Party.

Of the 248 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 122 to 70 and 56 were steady. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.61 percent to 1,801, the IMKB Services leapt 2.2 percent to 1,905 while the IMKB Financial eased 0.38 percent to 2,091.
Top actives were largely state-owned oil refiner Tupras, up 2,000 lira at 90,000 and flat steel maker Eregli, steady at 24,750 lira. They made up 15 percent of the total turnover.
The index representing tourism sector was the leading gainer with a 9.07 percent premium.
